clue.text: Moral science fiction film with HAL gripping in charge

parts.note: E.T. is Spielberg's science fiction film about a stranded alien

indicators.note: gripping means the computer's name holds the other piece inside it

explanation.surface: A film about an ethically dubious space computer: think 2001's HAL taking command.
explanation.walkthrough: HAL is the murderous computer in 2001: A Space Odyssey, which makes 'science fiction film' look like a pointer to that film rather than to E.T.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe conduct that follows principles of right and wrong; a synonym pair.

clue.text: European captures antelopes

parts.note: lands, as in landing a fish, means captures

explanation.surface: A European hunter bagging antelopes.
explanation.definitionFit: Elands are large African antelopes, examples of the general term.

clue.text: Harry has to bandage outbreak of spots? Not hard

indicators.note: to bandage means to wrap round, so the word has goes around the other piece

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: not means the letter for hard is left out

parts.note: a rash is an outbreak of spots on the skin
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone called Harry must cover up an eruption of spots, mildly.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry looks like a name but is the verb meaning to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry is to keep worrying or pestering someone, a synonym of the verb in the answer.

clue.text: Tailor cut a collar for summer?

indicators.note: to tailor is to alter or fashion, so these letters are refashioned

explanation.surface: A tailor trims a shirt collar for the warm season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summer' is one who sums, not the season; 'Tailor' looks like the subject but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A device for doing sums is literally a summer, with the question mark flagging the whimsical reading.

clue.text: Is without trousers? Not at first

indicators.note: not at first means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: slacks are casual trousers

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about whether someone is going without trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: If something lacks a thing it is without it; both phrases mean missing.

clue.text: Brilliant headwear — it goes with virtually everything

parts.note: a cap is a piece of headwear

indicators.note: virtually means almost, so the word for everything loses its last letter

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A fashion line: a great hat that matches any outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital is an old-fashioned British exclamation of approval meaning excellent, a synonym of brilliant.

clue.text: Character working with son getting hypocritical speech outside

indicators.note: outside means the word for hypocritical speech wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: cant is insincere, hypocritical talk
on means working, as in a machine being on
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sanctimonious figure working with his son delivers pious, insincere talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a person, but here it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A consonant is a kind of letter, and a letter is a written character.

clue.text: One's caught by hammer — agony!

indicators.note: caught by means held inside the other word

parts.note: to pan is to criticise severely, to hammer
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone hit by a hammer cries out in agony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hammer' is the verb for harsh criticism, not the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain and agony both mean physical or mental suffering; a synonym pair.

clue.text: Tramp almost certain to get riches

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to tread is to tramp heavily
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A vagrant is sure to strike it rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tramp' looks like a vagrant, but it is the verb for walking heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasure is a hoard of wealth, so it means riches.

clue.text: Trite remark with papa leaving room

indicators.note: leaving means the letter for papa goes out of the word

parts.note: a platitude is a trite, overused remark
P is papa in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A tired cliché delivered as dad walks out of the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'room' looks like a place, but it means scope or leeway.
explanation.definitionFit: Latitude means freedom of action, room to manoeuvre; a synonym in the sense of scope.

clue.text: Starts to paint roof in lockdown after a month

indicators.note: after says the picked letters come after the A
starts to these words means take the opening letter of each

explanation.surface: A home-improvement plan: begin painting the roof during lockdown, a month from now.
explanation.definitionFit: April is the fourth month of the year, an example of the general term.

clue.text: Happy to keep in Europe?

indicators.note: to keep means the word for happy holds the other piece within it

parts.note: content means happy or satisfied
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Brexit-flavoured question: would you be glad to stay in Europe?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks Europe as an example of the category rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Europe is one of the world's great landmasses, so it is an example of the category.

clue.text: Democrat is to swear I recalled no conversation

parts.note: to cuss is to swear

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word no is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A US politician insisting under oath that a talk never took place.
explanation.definitionFit: A discussion is a talk between people exchanging views; a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Returning in pants specifically — it attracts attention

indicators.note: Returning says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cheeky note that something about particular underwear draws the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The whispered sound is used to catch someone's notice discreetly, so it is a device for getting attention.

clue.text: Sky broadcast the operas, including Schumann's fifth

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so these letters are spread into a new order
fifth picks the fifth letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: Sky TV screens operas, among them one by Schumann.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sky' looks like the British TV company, but it is the heavens; 'including' adds the fifth letter, M, to the anagram pool.
explanation.definitionFit: The atmosphere is the envelope of air above the earth, which is loosely the sky.

clue.text: Made U-turn and faced ma, bewildered

indicators.note: bewildered means confused, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A child does an about-face to confront a baffled mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Manufactured means produced or made, especially by industrial process; a synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: University group of students with upper-class friend, strangely

parts.note: NUS is the National Union of Students, the UK students' body
U means upper-class in British usage
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A university society with a posh friend behaving oddly.
explanation.definitionFit: Unusually and strangely both describe something done in an odd or uncommon way.

clue.text: Changing gear with Mini's a headache

indicators.note: changing means altering, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Shifting gears in a Mini is a real pain.
explanation.walkthrough: A Mini is a small classic British car.
explanation.definitionFit: A migraine is a severe recurring kind of headache, an example of the general term.

clue.text: Focused attention on having kittens

definitions.meaning: to have emphasised a point is to have laid weight on it
having kittens is British slang for being very anxious or agitated

explanation.surface: A cat owner fretting over a pregnant cat.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is emphasised; the other, the idiom having kittens, means anxious and under strain.

clue.text: Launch I badly turn into dock, scratching stern

indicators.note: badly signals the letters are put together wrongly, rearranged
scratching the stern means removing the back end, so the word dock loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A boater confesses to a clumsy mooring that scraped the back of the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Launch' and 'stern' set a boating scene, but 'Launch' is a noun for a start; 'badly' scrambles TURN, INTO and DOC.
explanation.definitionFit: The launch of something is its opening or first presentation, and so is an introduction.

clue.text: Frank shocking court

parts.note: dire means dreadful or shocking

explanation.surface: A man named Frank appears in an outrageous trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name, but it is the adjective for candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank and the answer both mean straightforward and candid in speech.

clue.text: One manages The Telegraph crossword finally in competition, getting upset with nothing right

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so read backwards
in places that letter inside the word for competition

parts.note: a tie is a competition, as in an FA Cup tie

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of the word crossword

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A self-referential tale of a newspaper's crossword in a contest gone wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting upset' turns TIDE (TIE around D) into EDIT. An FA Cup tie is a knockout football match.
explanation.definitionFit: The person running a newspaper is its editor, the post at the head of The Telegraph.

clue.text: River fish — it's attached to the line, possibly

definitions.text: it's attached to the line, possibly

parts.note: an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: An angling scene: a river fish caught on a line.
explanation.definitionFit: On a fishing rod the spool that winds in the line is fixed to it; 'possibly' marks it as one example.

clue.text: Grew up timid? Well, unfortunately, wife's ignored

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so these letters are mixed up
is ignored means the letter for wife is left out of the word well

explanation.surface: A rueful question about whether one became a shy adult, while the spouse is overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grew up' reads as one phrase, but 'Grew' alone is the definition and 'up' joins the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To multiply is to increase in number, so grew is a synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: Ebbs and flows in government I described

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A politician describing how government power waxes and wanes.
explanation.definitionFit: The rise and fall of the sea is called its tides, each a flow and ebb.

clue.text: Market just open

definitions.meaning: a market or show held periodically

explanation.definitionFit: Three senses: a periodic market gathering, impartial treatment, and honest conduct.

clue.text: Set up of home delayed

parts.note: in means at home
stalled means held up or delayed

explanation.surface: A report that setting up a home has been held back.
explanation.definitionFit: Installed means put in place and made ready for use, which is to have set something up.

clue.text: Still time for tournament

parts.note: even can mean still, as in even better or still better

explanation.surface: Still time to enter the competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tournament is a sporting competition, which is called an event.

clue.text: Old tree likely to be hollow

parts.note: the elder is a small tree

indicators.note: to be hollow means emptied out, so only the outer letters of likely remain

explanation.surface: An old tree that is probably hollow inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderly describes people who are old or getting on in years; a synonym.

clue.text: Lieutenant in complete safety

indicators.note: in means the officer's abbreviation is placed inside the other word

parts.note: sheer means complete or utter, as in sheer nonsense

explanation.surface: An army officer reaching total safety.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelter is a place of protection from danger, so it means safety.
